title: Affine reduction and construction of profinite geometric fibres over a field
statement:
Let $k$ be a field, let $\Omega/k$ be a separable closure [def-pd-separable-closure], and put $G=\operatorname{Aut}_k(\Omega)$ with the Krull topology, whose identity neighbourhood basis consists of stabilizers of finite intermediate fields. Use small representatives as in [def-weil-size-convention]. A weakly etale $k$-scheme means an object of [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site], and affine spectra and their morphisms have the meaning of [def-weil-affine-spectrum].

Every affine open subscheme of an arbitrary weakly etale $k$-scheme is quasi-compact, quasi-separated and weakly etale over $k$. Every quasi-compact quasi-separated weakly etale $k$-scheme $U$ is affine. Its coordinate algebra $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$ is a directed union of finite etale $k$-subalgebras $B_i$, where finite etale means a finite product of finite separable field extensions. Conversely, the spectrum of any ind-etale $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-ind-etale-algebra] is a quasi-compact quasi-separated weakly etale $k$-scheme.

The group $G$ is profinite. For each ind-etale $k$-algebra $B$, let $F_k(B)=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(B,\Omega)$ and give it the topology generated by restriction to the finite discrete sets $\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(B_i,\Omega)$. The restriction map identifies $F_k(B)$ homeomorphically with their compatible-family inverse limit. It is a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected space, and $(g,f)\mapsto g\circ f$ is a continuous left $G$-action. If $B\ne0$, every finite-stage fibre is nonempty and every restriction map $F_k(B)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(B_i,\Omega)$ is surjective; $F_k(0)=\varnothing$. For every $k$-algebra map $\alpha:C\to B$ between ind-etale algebras, precomposition $f\mapsto f\circ\alpha$ is continuous and equivariant, and these maps form a contravariant functor. The construction uses all finite subalgebras and is independent of any cofinal choice of them.

source.place: Examples 4.1.4 and 4.1.10, pp. 27–28: affine reduction, finite fibres and their inverse-limit action.

proof.text: An affine open $V$ of a weakly etale $k$-scheme is weakly etale over $k$: weakly etale is Zariski local on the source [sk-lem-pe-weakly-etale-stability]. It is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Write $V=\operatorname{Spec}A$ using [def-weil-affine-spectrum]. By [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field], each finitely generated $k$-subalgebra of $A$ is finite etale. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product], these subalgebras are finite products of finite separable field extensions.

source.place: Example 4.1.4 and Lemma 4.1.6; Stacks 0CKR (more-algebra, lemma-class-weakly-etale-over-field), 00U3 (algebra, lemma-etale-over-field).

proof.text: Every prime of $A$ in step 1 is maximal. Indeed every element of the domain $A/\mathfrak p$ belongs to a finite-dimensional $k$-subalgebra. For a nonzero element its minimal polynomial over $k$ has nonzero constant term, so that polynomial expresses its inverse as a polynomial in the element. Thus $A/\mathfrak p$ is a field. If $x$ specializes to $y$ in an arbitrary weakly etale $k$-scheme, an affine neighbourhood of $y$ also contains $x$. In that affine neighbourhood all primes are maximal, so $x=y$. Hence every point is closed. Applying [lem-sfb-qcqs-zero-dimensional-affine] to a quasi-compact quasi-separated $U$ gives its affineness, including $U=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 0CKV, lemma-dimension-zero, final assertion; the preceding closed-point test is the elementary algebraic-domain argument from 0CKR.

proof.text: For affine $U$, put $B=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_U)$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-weak-etale-field]. The finitely generated $k$-subalgebras of $B$ form a directed family: combine finite generating sets for an upper bound, and every element belongs to the subalgebra it generates. Each is finite etale. Conversely [lem-weil-pbc-ind-etale-stability] makes any ind-etale $k$-algebra weakly etale; its spectrum is quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-affine-scheme-qcqs]. Applying the same field lemma shows that any such $B$ is the union of all its finite $k$-subalgebras, all of them finite etale by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product]. The chosen small representatives ensure these indices form a set.

The chosen separable closure $\Omega/k$ is Galois by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-closure-exists-galois]. Apply [lem-exc-galois-krull-finite-limit] with $K=k$: $G$ with its Krull topology is topologically isomorphic to the compatible-family limit of the finite groups $\operatorname{Gal}(L/k)$ over the nonempty directed set of finite Galois intermediate fields. By [lem-dl-a1-finite-group-limit-profinite] that limit is a compact Hausdorff totally disconnected topological group. This proves the asserted profiniteness of $G$ for the specified topology.

Write a finite subalgebra $B_i$ as $\prod_{a=1}^r L_a$ by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product]. A unital map from this product to the field $\Omega$ selects exactly one factor: the orthogonal idempotents must go to $0$ or $1$, and their sum is $1$. Its restriction on that factor is a $k$-embedding. By [lem-exc-etale-field-galois-classification] and the spectra/homomorphism correspondence of [def-weil-affine-spectrum], each set of embeddings $L_a\to\Omega$ is finite. Consequently $X_i=\operatorname{Hom}_{k\text{-alg}}(B_i,\Omega)$ is finite. If $B\ne0$, each $B_i\subset B$ is nonzero, hence $r\ge1$; [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed] supplies an embedding of each $L_a$ into $\Omega$, so $X_i\ne\varnothing$. For $B=0$ there is no unital map to $\Omega$, so $F_k(0)=\varnothing$.

source.place: Tag 03QR, lemma-sheaves-point, finite separable components; algebra Tag 00U3; fields Tag 09GU in its separable form recorded by the embedding node.

proof.text: For an inclusion $B_i\subseteq B_j$ and $t\in X_i$, let $e\in B_i$ be the idempotent selecting its field factor $L$. Its image in $B_j$ is nonzero by injectivity. In the product decomposition of $B_j$, choose a field factor $M$ where $e$ maps to $1$. The resulting unital map $L=eB_i\to M$ is injective. The extension $M/L$ is finite separable: $M/k$ is finite separable and a minimal polynomial over $L$ divides the separable minimal polynomial over $k$. Regard $\Omega$ as an $L$-extension using $t|_L$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-separable-extension-embeds-separably-closed] over $L$ to embed $M$ into $\Omega$ extending $t|_L$. Compose with $B_j\to M$. On $B_i$, $b=eb+(1-e)b$ goes to $t(eb)+0=t(b)$; thus $X_j\to X_i$ is surjective. The product decompositions are supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-algebra-over-field-product].

source.place: Tag 09GU, lemma-map-into-algebraic-closure, separable variant; finite product classification Tag 00U3 (algebra, lemma-etale-over-field).

proof.text: Restriction sends $f:B\to\Omega$ to a compatible family $(f_i)$. Conversely set $f(b)=f_i(b)$ for any $B_i$ containing $b$. Directedness and compatibility make this independent of $i$; choosing a single stage containing two elements checks addition and multiplication, and the common unit and $k$-structure are preserved. These operations are inverse bijections $F_k(B)\simeq\varprojlim_i X_i$. On both sides the topology is generated by the same finite-stage restrictions, so the bijection and its inverse are continuous. For $B\ne0$, steps 5 and 6 verify the finite nonempty and surjective-transition hypotheses of [lem-galois-inverse-limit-surjective]; that node makes every projection from the limit surjective, proving precisely the required surjectivity $F_k(B)\to X_i$.

source.place: Tag 086J, lemma-nonempty-limit, applied to the finite systems of fibres as in the cited node; the homomorphism/union identification is written out here.

proof.text: Give every finite $X_i$ its discrete topology. By [lem-weil-pbc-tychonoff-product-quasi-compact], $P=\prod_i X_i$ is compact. The compatible-family subset $L$ is closed: the equation $x_i=x_j|_{B_i}$ for each inclusion cuts out a clopen subset, since both coordinates have finite discrete targets. A cover of $L$ by relatively open sets extends to a cover of $P$ after adding $P\setminus L$, so compactness of $P$ gives a finite subcover of $L$. Distinct points of $L$ differ in some coordinate; the disjoint clopen coordinate cylinders separate them. Thus $L$ is Hausdorff, and a connected subset with two distinct points would be separated by such a cylinder, a contradiction. It is totally disconnected. The homeomorphism in step 7 gives all these properties to $F_k(B)$, also when it is empty.

source.place: Tag 08ZU, theorem-tychonov; the closed-subset and clopen-coordinate arguments give the special case of Tag 08ZY (lemma-profinite) directly.

proof.text: Postcomposition by $g\in G$ takes a $k$-algebra homomorphism to a $k$-algebra homomorphism, and $(gh)\circ f=g\circ(h\circ f)$ and $1\circ f=f$. For joint continuity at $(g_0,f_0)$, test a coordinate $B_i$. Put $t=f_0|_{B_i}$; its image is a finite intermediate field, since $B_i$ is a finite product of finite extensions and $t$ selects one field factor. The set of $f$ with $f|_{B_i}=t$ is open. For $g\in g_0\operatorname{Stab}_G(t(B_i))$ and such $f$, $(g\circ f)|_{B_i}=g_0\circ t$. This is an open neighbourhood in $G\times F_k(B)$ mapped into the desired coordinate cylinder, since the stabilizer is open by the specified Krull topology. These cylinders generate the topology; hence the action is continuous.

source.place: Example 4.1.10, profinite continuous G-sets; direct coordinate proof of continuity.

proof.text: For $\alpha:C\to B$ and a finite subalgebra $C_j\subset C$, its image $D=\alpha(C_j)$ is finite-dimensional over $k$ and is a subalgebra of $B$, so is one of the finite subalgebras used in step 3. The $C_j$ coordinate of $f\mapsto f\circ\alpha$ is restriction to $D$ followed by the map of finite discrete sets $\operatorname{Hom}_k(D,\Omega)\to\operatorname{Hom}_k(C_j,\Omega)$. Thus precomposition is continuous. Equivariance is the identity $g\circ(f\circ\alpha)=(g\circ f)\circ\alpha$. Precomposition with identity and composite algebra maps gives identity and composite maps in the reversed order, establishing the contravariant functor, including maps involving the zero algebra. Finally for any cofinal directed family of finite subalgebras, every finite subalgebra is contained in one of its stages. Restricting compatible families to this family is invertible by restricting from a larger chosen stage; a common upper bound proves independence. Each coordinate in either inverse is a restriction from one finite stage, hence continuous. The resulting homeomorphisms preserve each evaluation on $b\in B$ and the postcomposition action. This proves independence of the cofinal choice.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q74-2852b396c (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item's statement and all 10 steps in full, plus the statement of every cited node and stmt_dep. The delivery creates no new nodes and leaves the statement unchanged; it is one commit (item + report) on base 41d92ef. proof_deps equals the union of the uses. There is no cycle (checked over a 1072-node closure) and no SGA. Sources checked against the steps: Bhatt–Scholze Examples 4.1.4 and 4.1.10 (pp. 27-28), Stacks 0CKR (weakly étale over a field: finitely generated subalgebras are finite products of finite separable fields) and properties lemma-dimension-zero (in a quasi-separated dimension-0 scheme every quasi-compact open is affine). Step checks: (1) source locality, affine qcqs and the field/product nodes are used exactly as stated. (2) Primes are maximal because the minimal polynomial of an algebraic element of a domain has nonzero constant term; specialization is tested in an affine neighbourhood, so all points are closed, and the qcqs hypothesis of lem-sfb-qcqs-zero-dimensional-affine is met (empty case included). (3) Directed union and the ind-étale converse are correct. (4) Ω is Galois via the separable-closure node (2) with k'=k; the Krull-limit and finite-group-limit nodes give profiniteness. (5) A map to Ω selects one idempotent factor; finitely many embeddings via the classification node and the Spec Hom bijection; nonempty when B≠0. (6) The surjective-transition argument is correct: e maps to 1 in some factor M, M/L is separable, the embedding is taken over L via t, and b=eb+(1-e)b. (7) All hypotheses of lem-galois-inverse-limit-surjective are verified. (8)-(10) are genuinely elementary: closed subset of the Tychonoff product; joint continuity via g0·Gal(Ω/t(B_i)), reading 'stabilizer' as pointwise, the standard Krull basis; image of a finite subalgebra as an index; cofinal independence. Duplicate search: sibling nodes (tensor-fibres, covering-test), the geometric-field dense subsite, the zero-dim spectrum and the Galois-set decomposition all state different things. I accept the five declared tool_uses (weakly-étale stability, weak-étale field, ind-étale stability, étale-field product, étale-field Galois classification) as generic black boxes. The base-change and coefficient checks do not apply to this coefficient-free field-site lemma. Edge cases: B=0, k, Ω, a non-Galois finite field, several factors, imperfect separably closed k, an uncountable index. No fixes needed.
